judgment.notes: There are no E/M applications. Cauchy-Schwarz, the weak product rule, summability, bounded extension and smooth Fourier calculus apply with the actual L2, H1 and smooth-path conditions; see BG001–BG005. The coefficient series for B is summable since 2-2pstar=-9/7<-1. No L-infinity boundedness of S_t is assumed: its H1 isometry precedes the H1 embedding.

S001 proves the inverse-derivative and H1 product estimates and hence the H1 bound for J. S002 proves the B and Dinv P product bounds and the two A0 estimates; the A0 norm comparison has constant one since (1+k^2)^(-pstar)<=k^(-2) for nonzero k. All constants depend only on fixed convergent weight series. In S003 the phase derivative times (ir)^(-1)(is)^(-1) is 3ik, giving exactly the stated signs and factor 1/3; zero modes vanish by mean-zero and the outer derivative/projection. Smoothness justifies termwise calculus, and continuous piecewise smooth paths give cancelling internal endpoints. S004 uses the multiplier identity Dinv partial_x=P and commutation with S_t, proves symmetry and the Ctri identity on its defined smooth domain, and obtains the Fstage factor 1/6 by specializing F003 to constant paths. Density applies to the products for which bounds were proved.

The empty direct-input list is sufficient. S002 uses the earlier F001, and S004 uses the earlier F003; S003 is an independent local Fourier calculation. Arbitrary variables carry precisely the regularities in the corresponding output clauses. Fourier indices are bound summation indices. No existential witness, extra H, future fact, circular invocation of N005 or escaped local assumption occurs. Properties written in definitions are checked from their multiplier formulas rather than accepted as extra premises.

The supplied definitions, S001–S004 and the reviewed routine background suffice for the entire implication with no conditional inputs. Replay needs no producer body, source paper or absent project estimate. It establishes the stated bounds and the identities on their supplied smooth/piecewise smooth domains, together with bounded product extensions; it does not infer an unproved rough-input trilinear bound.

N005 states each estimate, time uniformity, the two-endpoint formula, the trilinear identification and the Fstage normalization. The supplied definitions fix the normalized Fourier/Sobolev norms, zero-mode conventions, pstar=23/14, and initial domains of B, J, Ctri and Fstage. In S002, <k> denotes the norm weight sqrt(1+k^2) from D003. The Ctri identity uses the smooth initial domain in D020, and Fstage uses D021; the final density clause extends the bounded products. All variables and endpoint conditions are supplied, without importing additional regularity claims.
